newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - HK stampede extends to first quarter of '97.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - HK stampede extends to first quarter of '97.

text.p: A slew of companies are expected to seek listings on the Hong Kong stock market in the first quarter of 1997, extending the stampede of initial public offerings (IPOs) in the territory, analysts said.
At least seven or eight companies are known in the market to be planning a first quarter listing, compared with six in the first quarter of last year, and more are expected, they said.

"Looking at the track record of 17 companies listed during the fourth quarter of 1996, I think there may be as many as 20 companies seeking listing in the first quarter this year," said one analyst at a local brokerage.
Analysts said a surge in the number of new listings is expected due to the market's strength and good fundamentals.
The blue-chip Hang Seng index, while a bit off the record levels of late November, is up 30 percent from the end of 1995.
"Many companies are trying to tap the strength of the market and that is seen to be the driving force leading to an increase in IPOs," said Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage.
Analysts said investors had gained confidence in IPOs following generally high subscription rates for share offers and strong performances in trading debuts in 1996.
There were 44 companies listed in 1996, compared with 26 in 1995, and total funds raised jumped to HK$26.70 billion from HK$7.64 billion the previous year.
According to research by Tai Fook Securities, new share offers were oversubscribed by an average of 70 times and the average price increase on the first day of trading for the shares was 21 percent.
But analysts said they expected mixed responses to future flotations and predicted subscription levels would flatten out a bit compared with those in 1996.

"The IPO market is expected be more exciting as more companies seek listing," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment. "But the hundreds of times oversubscription rates are unlikely to be repeated because investor interest will be diversified a bit by the greater variety of offerings."

Analysts said many manufacturing companies are seen launching IPOs in the first quarter, rushing to tap the market when it is strong, and more H-shares -- Hong Kong-listed shares in Chinese state-owned enterprises -- are also expected.

"It's a good timing for these IPOs due to current favourable market conditions," said Alex Wong, research analyst at Dharmala Securities. "We expect the overall operating profit margin of the industrial sector to improve because raw material prices are expected to be more stable in 1997."
Sentiment towards H-shares has also improved mainly due to anticipation of a possible interest rate cut in China.

Electrical and photographic products distributor Wah Lee Resources Holdings Ltd is offering 70 million new shares at HK$1.00 each. Its IPO is running from December 31 to January 6 and dealing in the shares is expected to begin on January 17.

Printing firm Cheong Ming Holdings Ltd is expected to launch an HK$80 million IPO this week, and souvenir maker Yip's Pota Holdings Ltd, plastic Christmas tree maker Boto Co Ltd, and Alpha Appliances are seen offering shares in the first quarter.
About five new H-share listings are also expected during the first quarter, compared with six in all of 1996.
China Eastern Airlines, which plans a dual listing in New York and Hong Kong, is seen starting its IPO in January or early February. China Southern Airlines is expected to follow suit.

Datang Power, which had delayed its dual listing plan in Hong Kong and London in December, is expected to come on to the market again shortly. Jiangsu Ninghu Expressway and Shenzhen Freeway are also expected to kick off their IPOs soon.
A couple of spinoffs are also expected during the period.
They include Champion Technology Holdings Ltd's unit Kantone Holdings Ltd, Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd's unit GZI Transport Ltd, and Leading Spirit (Holdings) Co Ltd's unit Konrowa.
